noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. the si-clause sets up a hypothetical condition, the conditional expresses...

noticing_prompts.q: How do you form 'tuviera'? Start from the preterite of 'tener' and explain each step.
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. tener → preterite 3rd pl. 'tuvieron' → remove -ron → add -ra...

structured_input.sentence: Si tuviéramos más tiempo, terminaríamos el proyecto hoy.
structured_input.question: What tense pair is used and what does it express?
options: Imperfect subjunctive + conditional — a hypothetical/unlikely situation in the present or future
Present subjunctive + future — a probable condition
Imperfect subjunctive + imperfect — a past habitual action
Present indicative + conditional — a likely real condition
structured_input.feedback: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional = a hypothetical condition (contrary to present fact or unlikely). It means 'If we had more time (which we don't), we would finish…'

structured_input.sentence: El director pedía que los empleados llegaran puntualmente.
structured_input.question: Why is 'llegaran' in the imperfect subjunctive?
options: Because the main verb 'pedía' is in the imperfect — past tense triggers imperfect subjunctive in the subordinate clause
Because 'llegar' is an irregular verb that always uses subjunctive
Because 'pedir' always requires imperfect subjunctive
Because it refers to a habitual action in the past
structured_input.feedback: The rule of 'sequence of tenses': when the main verb is in a past tense (pedía), the subordinate subjunctive must also be past (llegaran).

quiz.sentence: Si yo ___ (ser) el jefe, cambiaría muchas cosas.
quiz.feedback_why: Si + imperfect subjunctive: 'ser' → 3rd pl preterite 'fueron' → remove -ron → fuera/fuese. Both forms are accepted.

quiz.sentence: Quería que tú ___ (venir) a la reunión.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Quería' (past) → subordinate clause uses imperfect subjunctive. 'Venir' → 3rd pl preterite 'vinieron' → remove -ron → viniera. Tú = vinieras.

quiz.sentence: ___ (yo / querer) un café con leche, por favor. (polite formal request)
quiz.feedback_why: 'Quisiera' (imperfect subjunctive of querer) is a set phrase for polite requests, equivalent to 'I would like'. Very common in formal/service contexts.

rules.title: Passive Voice — ser + participle and se pasiva
rules.title_es: Voz pasiva — ser + participio y se pasiva
rules.explanation: Spanish has two main passive constructions. (1) **Passive with ser**: subject + **ser** (conjugated for tense) + past participle (agrees in gender/number) + **por** + agent. Example: *El informe fue escrito por la directora.* (2) **Se pasiva**: **se** + 3rd person verb (singular or plural depending on subject). Example: *Se venden apartamentos.* The se-pasiva is more common in everyday speech when the agent is unknown or unimportant. The ser-passive is more formal and common in written language.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: ¿Saben que el nuevo parque **fue inaugurado** ayer por el alcalde?

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Sí, lo vi en las noticias. También **se anunciaron** nuevas rutas de metro.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: En este barrio **se construyen** muchos edificios últimamente. **Se espera** que los precios suban.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: La nueva ley **fue aprobada** por el parlamento la semana pasada. Todo **se está cambiando** muy rápido.

noticing_prompts.q: Compare 'fue inaugurado por el alcalde' and 'se anunciaron nuevas rutas'. What information does each structure include or omit?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. the ser-passive includes the agent 'por', while se-pasiva...

noticing_prompts.q: In 'Se construyen muchos edificios', why is the verb plural? What is the grammatical subject?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. the subject is 'muchos edificios' which is plural, so...

structured_input.sentence: El contrato fue firmado por ambas partes.
structured_input.question: What is the structure of this passive sentence?
options: Subject 'El contrato' + ser (past) + past participle 'firmado' + agent 'por ambas partes'
Subject 'ambas partes' + ser (past) + past participle + destination
Reflexive se + verb in passive form + agent
Impersonal se + verb + indirect object
structured_input.feedback: 'El contrato' is the subject (what was signed); 'fue' is ser in preterite; 'firmado' agrees with 'el contrato' (masculine singular); 'por ambas partes' names the agent.

structured_input.sentence: Se habla español en más de 20 países.
structured_input.question: Why is 'habla' singular here?
options: Because 'español' (the grammatical subject in se-pasiva) is singular
Because 'se' is always singular
Because the verb is impersonal and never changes
Because países is the indirect object, not the subject
structured_input.feedback: In se-pasiva, the verb agrees with the grammatical subject. 'Español' is singular → 'se habla'. If it were 'Se hablan varios idiomas', 'idiomas' (plural) would require 'hablan'.

quiz.sentence: Los documentos ___ (preparar) por el equipo legal.
quiz.feedback_why: Ser-passive: 'fueron' (preterite of ser, 3rd pl) + 'preparados' (participle, masculine plural to agree with 'los documentos').

quiz.sentence: ___ alquilan apartamentos en esta zona.
quiz.feedback_why: Se-pasiva: 'Se alquilan apartamentos' = 'Apartments are rented / Apartments for rent'. 'Alquilan' is plural because 'apartamentos' is the subject.

quiz.sentence: La novela ___ (escribir) en solo tres semanas por la autora.
quiz.feedback_why: Ser-passive: 'fue' (singular, for 'la novela') + 'escrita' (feminine to agree with 'la novela').

rules.title_en: Passive Voice — ser + participle and se pasiva

rules.title: Relative Clauses — que, quien, el que, cuyo
rules.title_es: Cláusulas de relativo — que, quien, el que, cuyo
rules.explanation: Relative clauses modify a noun (the antecedent). Key pronouns: **que** — most common, for people and things; **quien/quienes** — only for people, usually in non-restrictive clauses or after prepositions; **el que / la que / los que / las que** — when you need gender/number agreement or after prepositions; **lo que** — refers to an idea or clause, not a noun; **cuyo/a/os/as** — possessive relative (whose), agrees with the noun it modifies, not the owner. Restrictive clauses (no comma) vs non-restrictive clauses (with comma, adds extra info).

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: El colega **con quien** trabajo es el **que** más sabe de finanzas.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: ¿Es el chico **cuyo** padre trabaja en el banco? Le conocí en la conferencia.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Sí, exacto. **Lo que** más me impresiona es su capacidad de análisis.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: La empresa para **la que** trabajan tiene muy buena reputación, **lo que** es importante.

noticing_prompts.q: Why is 'quien' used in 'el colega con quien trabajo' instead of 'que'?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. after prepositions (con, de, para...) with people, 'quien' is preferred over...

noticing_prompts.q: In 'cuyo padre trabaja', why is it 'cuyo' and not 'cuyos' or 'cuya'?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'cuyo' agrees with the noun it modifies, which is 'padre' = masculine singular...

structured_input.sentence: La empresa para la que trabajo tiene 500 empleados.
structured_input.question: Why is 'la que' used instead of just 'que'?
options: Because 'para' (a preposition) requires a pronoun with an article; 'que' alone cannot follow prepositions
Because 'empresa' is feminine and requires a feminine relative pronoun
Because 'la que' always replaces 'que' in formal writing
Because 'para que' has a different meaning (purpose clause)
structured_input.feedback: After prepositions (para, con, de, en…), you need 'el/la que' or 'quien' instead of bare 'que'. 'Para que' would mean 'so that' (purpose), which changes the meaning entirely.

structured_input.sentence: Lo que dijiste ayer me hizo pensar mucho.
structured_input.question: What does 'lo que' refer to?
options: The whole idea or thing that you said — referring to an action/concept rather than a specific noun
A masculine singular noun mentioned previously
The person who said something
The time when you said something
structured_input.feedback: 'Lo que' = 'what' / 'that which'. It refers to an abstract idea or action, not a specific noun. It is neuter and invariable.

quiz.sentence: La persona ___ te recomendé es experta en marketing.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Que' is the standard relative pronoun for people when there is no preposition. Restrictive clause (no comma).

quiz.sentence: Es una empresa ___ empleados trabajan en más de 30 países.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Cuyo/a/os/as' expresses possession. Agrees with 'empleados' (masculine plural) → cuyos.

quiz.sentence: No entiendo ___ quieres decir con eso.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Lo que' = 'what' referring to an abstract concept or idea, not a specific noun.

rules.title_en: Relative Clauses — que, quien, el que, cuyo

rules.title: Pluperfect — The past before the past
rules.title_es: Pluscuamperfecto — El pasado anterior al pasado
rules.explanation: The **pluperfect** (pluscuamperfecto) expresses an action that was completed **before another past action**. It is formed with the imperfect of **haber** (había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían) + the **past participle**. It corresponds to English 'had done'. Common use: narrating past events in sequence, explaining background by the time something else happened, and in subordinate clauses after 'cuando', 'después de que', 'como', 'porque' etc. with past context.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Cuando llegué a la fiesta, la mayoría de la gente ya **se había marchado**.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: ¿De verdad? Yo creía que **habías dicho** que empezaba a las nueve.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Sí, pero se retrasó. Para cuando me avisaron, ya **había perdido** el autobús.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Qué mala suerte. ¿Y la comida? ¿**Habían** ya **terminado** todo?

noticing_prompts.q: In 'cuando llegué, ya se había marchado' — which action happened first? How does the pluperfect mark this sequence?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'había marchado' happened before 'llegué' because...

noticing_prompts.q: What are the two components of 'había perdido'? What tense is each?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'había' is imperfect of haber + 'perdido' is past participle of...

structured_input.sentence: Cuando llegué al aeropuerto, el avión ya había despegado.
structured_input.question: Which event happened first — arriving at the airport or the plane departing?
options: The plane departing — pluperfect signals it was already completed before arrival
Arriving at the airport — simple past always precedes pluperfect
Both happened at the same time — 'ya' signals simultaneity
Arriving at the airport — it was the cause of the plane's departure
structured_input.feedback: Pluperfect = past before the past. 'Había despegado' (pluperfect) → happened before 'llegué' (simple past). The plane had already taken off when you arrived.

structured_input.sentence: No había dormido bien porque había tomado demasiado café.
structured_input.question: What sequence of events does this sentence describe?
options: Drinking too much coffee (first) → not sleeping well (second, later in the past)
Not sleeping well (first) → drinking coffee as a result
Both actions happening at the same time
A hypothetical situation that did not happen
structured_input.feedback: Both verbs are in the pluperfect, giving them the same relative time level — they are both background past. The causal relationship (porque) tells us the coffee came first logically.

quiz.sentence: Cuando llamé, ya ___ (salir / ella).
quiz.feedback_why: Pluperfect: 'había' (3rd singular of haber imperfect) + 'salido' (past participle of salir). She had already left when you called.

quiz.sentence: Nos fuimos a casa porque ___ (terminar / el concierto).
quiz.feedback_why: The concert ending happened before they left. Pluperfect: 'había terminado'.

quiz.sentence: ¿___ (tú / ver) esa película antes de ayer?
quiz.feedback_why: 'Habías' (imperfect of haber, 2nd singular) + 'visto' (irregular participle of ver).

rules.title_en: Pluperfect — The past before the past

rules.title: Future Perfect — Completed future actions
rules.explanation: The **futuro perfecto** expresses an action that **will have been completed** by a certain point in the future, or it expresses **probability about the past**. Formed with: future of **haber** (habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán) + **past participle**. Uses: (1) Action before a future reference: *Para el lunes, habré terminado el informe.* (2) Probable past: *Habrá salido ya.* (It has probably already left.) This dual use — future completion and past speculation — makes it a sophisticated tense.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Para fin de año, **habremos completado** los tres proyectos.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Espero que sí. Para entonces yo ya **habré acabado** el máster.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: ¿No ha llegado todavía Ana? **Habrá** tenido algún problema en el metro.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Sí, o **habrá** olvidado la reunión. Eso también le **habrá pasado** antes.

noticing_prompts.q: In 'Para fin de año, habremos completado', what does 'para fin de año' tell us about the temporal relationship between the future perfect action and the reference point?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'para' sets a deadline — the action will be completed before or by...

noticing_prompts.q: 'Habrá tenido algún problema' — does this refer to something in the future or the past? How can you tell?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. it refers to a present/past probability because the speaker is speculating about why...

structured_input.sentence: Para cuando llegues, ya habremos comido.
structured_input.question: What two future events are described and which comes first?
options: Eating comes first (habremos comido), then your arrival (llegues) — we will have already eaten by the time you arrive
Your arrival comes first, then eating
Both happen at the same time in the future
Eating is a hypothesis that depends on whether you arrive
structured_input.feedback: Future perfect establishes a sequence: 'habremos comido' will be completed before 'llegues'. The present subjunctive 'llegues' is used in subordinate temporal clauses about the future.

structured_input.sentence: No contesta. Habrá salido a comer.
structured_input.question: What function does 'habrá salido' serve here?
options: Speculation about a past or present action — 'She has probably gone out to eat'
A definite prediction about the future
A conditional statement about eating
A command or obligation to go out
structured_input.feedback: When future perfect is used without a future time reference, it expresses probability about the past or present: 'Habrá salido' = 'She's probably/must have gone out'.

quiz.sentence: Para el próximo lunes, nosotros ___ (entregar) todos los documentos.
quiz.feedback_why: Future perfect: 'habremos' (nosotros, future of haber) + 'entregado' (past participle of entregar).

quiz.sentence: No encuentro las llaves. Las ___ (dejar / yo) en la oficina.
quiz.feedback_why: Future perfect for past probability: 'habré dejado' = 'I must have left them / I've probably left them' at the office.

quiz.sentence: ¿Cuántos libros ___ (leer / él) para el final del año?
quiz.feedback_why: 'Habrá' (3rd singular, future of haber) + 'leído' (past participle of leer, with written accent).

rules.title: Advanced Subjunctive — Sequence and nuance
rules.explanation: At C2 level, the subjunctive is used across all tenses with precision. Key advanced patterns: (1) **Concordancia de tiempos** (sequence of tenses): main clause tense determines which subjunctive tense follows — present/future → present subjunctive; past/conditional → imperfect subjunctive; perfect → perfect subjunctive. (2) **Subjuntivo en relativas**: with indefinite or negative antecedents — *Busco a alguien que hable chino.* (3) **Aunque + subjunctive** for hypothetical concession vs. indicative for known facts. (4) **Por + adj/adv + que + subjunctive**: *Por mucho que insistas, no cambiaré de opinión.*

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Necesitamos un candidato que **tenga** experiencia internacional y que **hable** tres idiomas.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: **Aunque sea** difícil de encontrar, no vamos a bajar el listón. Por mucho que **cueste**, vale la pena.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: Ojalá **hayamos tomado** la decisión correcta con el candidato anterior.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Buscaremos hasta que **encontremos** a la persona idónea, **aunque nos lleve** meses.

noticing_prompts.q: In 'Busco a alguien que hable chino', why is 'hable' in the subjunctive? How would the meaning change if you used 'habla'?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. subjunctive here because the person is hypothetical/unknown; indicative would mean...

noticing_prompts.q: Compare 'aunque sea difícil' and 'aunque es difícil'. What is the difference in what the speaker assumes?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'sea' (subjunctive) = I'm not sure it is; 'es' (indicative) = I know it is...

structured_input.sentence: Quiero un apartamento que tenga terraza.
structured_input.question: Why is 'tenga' in the subjunctive?
options: Because the apartment is hypothetical — no specific apartment has been identified yet
Because 'querer' always requires subjunctive
Because 'apartamento' is an indefinite noun
Because 'terraza' triggers subjunctive in subordinate clauses
structured_input.feedback: When the antecedent is unknown/non-existent, use the subjunctive in the relative clause. You are describing desired characteristics, not a specific identified apartment.

structured_input.sentence: Por más que estudies, si no descansas, no rendirás bien.
structured_input.question: What does 'por más que + subjunctive' express?
options: A concessive clause — no matter how much you study, the result is still the same
A condition — if you study more, you will do well
A purpose clause — you study so that you can do well
A temporal clause — as you are studying more
structured_input.feedback: 'Por más que + subjunctive' = 'no matter how much'. It concedes the effort but denies that it changes the outcome. Equivalent patterns: por mucho que, por bien que, por más que.

quiz.sentence: Buscan empleados que ___ (tener) al menos cinco años de experiencia.
quiz.feedback_why: Subjunctive in relative clause with indefinite antecedent: 'empleados que tengan...' — no specific employees identified yet.

quiz.sentence: Esperaba que ellos ___ (llegar) antes de la cena.
quiz.feedback_why: Sequence of tenses: 'esperaba' (imperfect) → imperfect subjunctive 'llegaran/llegasen'.

quiz.sentence: ___ mucho que lo intentes, no podrás convencerle.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Por más/mucho que + subjunctive' = no matter how much. Fixed concessive structure.

rules.title: Discourse Markers — Connecting ideas in speech and writing
rules.title_es: Marcadores del discurso — Conectar ideas al hablar y escribir
rules.explanation: **Discourse markers** (marcadores del discurso) are words and phrases that organize, connect, and signal relationships between ideas. They work at the text level, not the sentence level. Key categories: **Addition**: además, asimismo, incluso, por añadidura. **Contrast**: sin embargo, no obstante, aunque, si bien, ahora bien, a pesar de (que). **Cause**: puesto que, dado que, ya que (explaining), debido a. **Consequence**: por lo tanto, por consiguiente, en consecuencia, de ahí que (+subj). **Reformulation**: es decir, o sea, en otras palabras, a saber. **Ordering**: en primer lugar, por un lado…por otro, finalmente, en definitiva. Register matters: 'sin embargo' and 'no obstante' are formal equivalents of 'pero'.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: El proyecto tiene ventajas evidentes. **Sin embargo**, los costes son elevados. **Además**, el plazo es muy ajustado.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: **Dado que** los inversores ya han comprometido fondos, no podemos retirarnos. **Por consiguiente**, debemos seguir adelante.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: **En otras palabras**, no tenemos alternativa. **No obstante**, podríamos renegociar los plazos.

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: **En definitiva**, la decisión es arriesgada pero necesaria. **De ahí que** el equipo esté tan preocupado.

noticing_prompts.q: What is the difference between 'pero', 'sin embargo', and 'no obstante'? Can they always be substituted for each other?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'pero' is informal, 'sin embargo' is formal; 'sin embargo' usually starts a new sentence while 'pero' connects within...

noticing_prompts.q: Notice 'de ahí que el equipo esté'. Why is 'esté' in the subjunctive after 'de ahí que'?
noticing_prompts.placeholder: e.g. 'de ahí que' expresses consequence and always triggers...

structured_input.sentence: No teníamos presupuesto. Por lo tanto, cancelamos el viaje.
structured_input.question: What logical relationship does 'por lo tanto' express?
options: Consequence — the cancellation is the result of the budget problem
Contrast — despite the budget, they cancelled
Addition — an extra piece of information
Condition — if there is no budget, then they will cancel
structured_input.feedback: 'Por lo tanto' / 'por consiguiente' / 'en consecuencia' all express logical consequence. The first clause is the cause, the second is the result.

structured_input.sentence: Puesto que ya conoces la situación, no hace falta explicarlo.
structured_input.question: What does 'puesto que' express?
options: Cause/reason — since/because you already know the situation
Condition — if you know the situation
Contrast — although you know the situation
Concession — even though you know the situation
structured_input.feedback: 'Puesto que', 'dado que', 'ya que' all introduce a cause or reason (more formal than 'porque'). They present the reason as already known or obvious.

quiz.sentence: La propuesta es interesante, ___ tiene varios puntos débiles.
quiz.feedback_why: Contrast connector: 'sin embargo' or 'no obstante' introduce a contrasting idea in formal register. Both accepted.

quiz.sentence: ___ que la economía mejora, podríamos invertir más.
quiz.feedback_why: 'Dado que' / 'Puesto que' = since / given that (causal). Formal alternatives to 'porque'.

quiz.sentence: El sistema es complejo, ___ requiere formación especializada.
quiz.feedback_why: Consequence connector. 'Por consiguiente', 'por lo tanto', and 'en consecuencia' all express that what follows is the result.

rules.title_en: Discourse Markers — Connecting ideas in speech and writing

rules.title: Reported Speech — Indirect style tense shifts
rules.title_es: Estilo indirecto — Cambios de tiempo en el discurso referido
rules.explanation: **Reported speech** (estilo indirecto) requires systematic tense shifts when the reporting verb is in the past. Present → imperfect; preterite → pluperfect; future → conditional; present subjunctive → imperfect subjunctive; imperative → imperfect subjunctive. Pronouns, time expressions, and place references also shift: 'ahora' → 'entonces', 'aquí' → 'allí', 'este' → 'ese/aquel', 'mañana' → 'al día siguiente', 'ayer' → 'el día anterior'. When the reporting verb is in the present, tenses do NOT shift.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN
context_dialogue.text: Ana dijo «Llegaré mañana y traeré los documentos.»

context_dialogue.speaker: MIA
context_dialogue.text: O sea, Ana dijo que **llegaría** al día siguiente y que **traería** los documentos.

context_dialogue.speaker: DAN

structured_input.sentence: Dijo «Estoy cansado.» → Dijo que ___ cansado.
structured_input.question: Which tense replaces the present 'estoy' in reported speech with past reporting verb?
options: Imperfect: 'estaba' — present shifts to imperfect in past reported speech
Preterite: 'estuvo' — present always shifts to preterite
Present subjunctive: 'esté' — dijo requires subjunctive
No change: 'está' — present tense never changes
structured_input.feedback: Present (estoy) → imperfect (estaba) in past reported speech. 'Dijo que estaba cansado.'

structured_input.sentence: Prometió «No lo haré.» → Prometió que no lo ___.
structured_input.question: The future 'haré' shifts to which tense in reported speech?
options: Conditional 'haría' — future shifts to conditional in past reported speech
Imperfect subjunctive 'hiciera' — future always shifts to imperfect subjunctive
Present 'hará' — the tense does not change
Pluperfect 'había hecho' — future is already past from the speaker's perspective
structured_input.feedback: Future (haré) → conditional (haría) in past reported speech. 'Prometió que no lo haría.'

quiz.sentence: Dijo «Tengo hambre.» → Dijo que ___ hambre.
quiz.feedback_why: Present 'tengo' → imperfect 'tenía' in past reported speech.

quiz.sentence: Nos preguntó «¿Han terminado?» → Nos preguntó si ___ terminado.
quiz.feedback_why: Present perfect 'han terminado' → pluperfect 'habíamos terminado' in past reported speech. Full answer: 'si habíamos terminado'.

quiz.sentence: Me dijo «Llama mañana.» → Me dijo que ___ al día siguiente.
quiz.feedback_why: Imperative 'llama' → imperfect subjunctive 'llamara/llamase' in reported speech. 'Mañana' → 'al día siguiente'.
